newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco, Teck, Cominco in talks.
newsitem.headline: Codelco, Teck, Cominco in talks.

text.p: Canadian mining companies Teck Corp and Cominco Ltd are in talks for joint copper exploration deals with Chile's state copper giant Codelco, said a senior Teck official.
Teck and Cominco, which have a joint prospecting program in Chile, hope to sign a one agreement with Codelco before year-end, said Bob Young general manager of Minera Teck Chile.
"Things are going back and forth between our and Codelco's lawyers," Young told Reuters in an interview by telephone.
"There's no date fixed, but hopefully we'll have one (deal) by the end of the year."
The companies are also close to clinching an agreement on exploring a second Codelco deposit and have several other deals with the state corporation in the pipeline, he said.
Young declined to identify the sites involved but said they were all copper deposits at a basic stage of exploration.
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, is keen to carry out deals with private companies to allow them to prospect on land which is either too risky or too small to be of use to the company.
Private firms which have linked up with Codelco include another Canadian mining company, Noranda Inc, which has signed an agreement to explore the Guacate property.

Cominco and Teck spend jointly around $5 million a year in exploration in Chile, said Young. Cominco funds two-thirds of the investment with the rest paid for by Teck -- Cominco's majority shareholder.
Vancouver-based Teck has recently signed a $250 million deal with Anglo American to build a gold mine at the Marte-Lobo deposit in northern Chile.
Teck will invest $2-2.5 million over the next couple of years exploring around the Marte-Lobo site, he said.
The company is also carrying out exploration in Argentina with a smaller Canadian mining company Mansfield Minerals.
The companies have recently started drilling work at the Cerro Samenta copper deposit in Argentina's nothern Salta province, he said.
"The geology looks good, but we need to look closely at the grades," said Young.
The drilling program should last at least 4-5 months, he said.
Teck, which owns 30 percent of Chilean copper mine Quebrada Blanca, invests around $12 million a year in exploration in Latin America. -- Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212
